title: Use SQLite with FTS5 for project memory
body: The live project memory store is a SQLite database scoped by a stable project key. FTS5 supplies lexical retrieval and typed edges supply graph expansion. This avoids a separate graph database or vector service while keeping recall local and fast. Curated knowledge is exported as JSONL rather than committing the database.

citations.excerpt: The live knowledge store is a SQLite database in the OpenCode data directory, scoped by a stable project key.

title: Use optimistic writes with earned auto-injection
body: Agents can write claims freely, but only verified or cited claims auto-inject in normal scopes. Inferred claims are queryable through explicit recall and must be confirmed by a human or an independent, rejection-leaning verifier before auto-injection. Disputed and stale claims require explicit recall.

citations.excerpt: Agents may write claims freely, but auto-injection is earned.
Approved as the project memory injection policy.

title: Model claims and entities as separate node kinds
body: Entity nodes represent components, concepts, documents, sources, and sessions. Claim nodes represent facts, decisions, gotchas, patterns, and runbooks. Claims attach to entities and sources through typed edges. This allows each claim to carry its own citations, confidence, conflicts, and version history instead of hiding observations inside an entity.

citations.excerpt: A claim can carry multiple citations, can be contested by another claim, and can be superseded without losing its history.

title: Sample audits with 3 percent uniform and 7 percent risk-weighted
body: Auto-inject-eligible claims are audited with a 3% uniform random sample and a 7% risk-weighted sample. The uniform sample estimates defect rate; the risk sample catches likely bad claims first. Deterministic citation checks run on every write, and disputes, stale citations, and verification failures trigger audits directly.

citations.excerpt: Auto-inject-eligible claims are audited with a 3% uniform random sample and a 7% risk-weighted sample.

title: Require verified evidence in strict scopes
body: Normal scopes allow cited and verified claims to auto-inject. Strict scopes such as auth, payments, production infrastructure, and migrations require verified evidence or explicit recall. When scope inference is uncertain, the stricter policy wins.

citations.excerpt: Strict scopes such as auth, payments, infra/prod, and migrations require verified evidence or explicit recall.

title: Run automatic recall from the prompt hook
body: Automatic recall runs once per admitted user prompt, not on every tool continuation. It retrieves only auto-inject-eligible cards under a small token budget, records the injected node IDs, and persists the block as a session instruction entry when available. The context hook is a fallback for runtimes without session instruction entries.

citations.excerpt: Automatic recall runs from the prompt hook, and the recalled block is persisted as a session instruction entry when available.

title: Return compact evidence cards with provenance
body: Recall returns compact cards containing a node ID, kind, basis, status, confidence, a short body, scope, sources, and related node IDs. It does not synthesize an answer with a second model. The calling agent reasons over evidence and can call memory_get or memory_neighbors for more detail.

citations.excerpt: Recall returns compact evidence cards containing a node ID, kind, basis, status, confidence, a short body, scope, sources, and related node IDs.

title: bun:sqlite and node:sqlite need a shared adapter
body: The OpenCode server runs on Bun and provides bun:sqlite. The CLI and tests run on Node and use node:sqlite. The storage layer must use a small adapter that tries bun:sqlite first and falls back to node:sqlite, because better-sqlite3 is not supported in Bun.

citations.excerpt: The plugin runs in OpenCode's Bun server and uses bun:sqlite. The CLI and tests run on Node and use Node's built-in node:sqlite.

title: Inferred claims must not auto-inject
body: An inferred claim is useful context but is not evidence. It can be recalled explicitly, where it is labelled unverified, but it must be promoted to cited or verified before automatic injection. A material revision resets the promotion so a benign claim cannot be verified and then silently rewritten.

title: Memory store
body: The MemoryStore owns persistence, retrieval, write validation, deduplication, conflict edges, audit records, injection logs, and export. It has no OpenCode imports, so the CLI, tests, and plugin all use the same core through a small interface.

citations.excerpt: The MemoryStore owns persistence, retrieval, write validation, deduplication, conflict edges, audit records, injection logs, and export.

title: Earned injection
body: Earned injection is the policy that a claim may be stored immediately but must accumulate evidence or confirmation before it enters the ambient context automatically. It separates contribution from trust and keeps the agent's context budget for claims with provenance.

citations.excerpt: This preserves broad contribution without letting every hypothesis enter the ambient context.

title: Export curated memory as a deterministic JSONL bundle
body: The local SQLite file is the live store and is not committed. A memory export writes nodes, versions, edges, sources, citations, and a manifest as deterministic JSONL so the knowledge can be reviewed, backed up, or shared. Import must revalidate citations and re-evaluate injection eligibility locally.

citations.excerpt: Curated knowledge can be exported as a deterministic JSONL bundle for review, backup, or sharing.
